segments.text: After brushing his teeth, Gummy drinks orange juice - and it's suddenly bitter.
But the orange juice itself hasn't changed at all.
The foam in toothpaste briefly blocks his sweet taste cells.
It also disrupts what usually keeps his bitter taste cells calm.
Orange juice always has a touch of bitterness hidden in its sweetness.
Right now, though, the sweetness is weak and the bitterness stands out.
Check again - the orange juice hasn't changed one bit.
It's the toothpaste's foam that dulls sweetness and sharpens bitterness.
